objective: Add truthful observability and cross-system synchronization semantics across backend, PostgreSQL, MQTT, firmware, WebSocket, and frontend without making diagnostics authoritative.

acceptance.criterion: Observability remains diagnostic; authoritative state remains in its declared domain.
Documentation distinguishes deployed infrastructure from proposed integrations.
Supported cross-system operations preserve correlation_id while keeping request_id, trace_id, command_id, event_id, and config version distinct.
Supported backend boundaries propagate trace context without using it as business identity or authorization.
acceptance.verification: Backend observability tests and source inspection

acceptance.criterion: Synchronization-sensitive observations have explicit freshness rules and stale observations do not become current.
acceptance.verification: topic_last_seen regression test and frontend sync tests

acceptance.criterion: Desired, observed/applied, cached, transport, and synchronization state are distinguished where implemented.
Delayed or out-of-order observations cannot overwrite newer authoritative state.
Stable identities are used to prevent duplicate logical processing where implemented.
acceptance.verification: Backend lifecycle and shared contract tests

acceptance.criterion: Actual delivery guarantees are documented; no unsupported exactly-once guarantee is claimed.
Retry/reconciliation behavior is bounded and restart-safe where implemented.
acceptance.verification: Backend lifecycle tests and source inspection

acceptance.criterion: Outbox use is an explicit architecture decision; no unsupported outbox claim is made.
WebSocket reconnect recovers from authoritative query state rather than treating the stream as complete history.
MQTT reconnect restores subscriptions without fabricating device state.
acceptance.verification: Backend MQTT lifecycle tests and source inspection

acceptance.criterion: Liveness, dependency readiness, device health, and synchronization health remain distinct.
New metric labels have bounded cardinality and do not contain correlation/request/command IDs or arbitrary payloads.
Secrets are not added to logs, metrics, traces, diagnostics, or synchronization metadata.
Backend and frontend caches remain non-authoritative and recover freshness/version semantics where required.
acceptance.verification: Frontend sync tests and source inspection

acceptance.criterion: Executable tests cover applicable cross-system success, duplication, staleness, ordering, failure, and recovery behavior.
acceptance.verification: Repository test suites and evidence contract

acceptance.criterion: Existing P1.1-P1.9 authorization, lifecycle, safety, state, journal, API/cache, context, and schema invariants remain intact.
acceptance.verification: Existing focused tests plus shared/backend/frontend validation

acceptance.criterion: Acceptance evidence distinguishes PASS, BLOCKED, and unverified runtime claims.
